claude.rationale: gap_45 = 1: the deal creates and co-owns a new customer-facing asset (T4, ~90,000 hp of compression expanding capacity from 1.5 to 2.0 Bcf/d), with Enterprise financing and constructing it, while the operating processes/personnel that run the system explicitly remain with Jonah/TEPPCO — "the operating processes and personnel that run the system remain with Jonah/TEPPCO" (Sections 1(b), 2, 4) — a product-vs-process split at closing. gap_mitigated = yes: the mismatch is contractually absorbed via the Subscription mechanism, the TEPPCO reimbursement/adjustment option (Section 1(c)), and an arbitration fallback fixing relative interests (Sections 1(e), 3, 10). gap_56 = 0: the operating organization is not re-engineered apart from its people — Jonah is to "preserve intact its present business organization, keep available the services of its present officers and employees" (Section 4), so processes and their people stay together. Both are coded from the letter-of-intent closing structure only; because the JV vehicle and ownership split are deferred to the definitive agreement, T2/T3 are partial and the ownership is a subset of the combined system.

gemini.rationale: The transaction structurally separates the funding and construction of the expansion asset (Enterprise) from the operating processes and personnel (TEPPCO/Jonah), creating a gap between the asset's creation/ownership and its operational execution (gap_45). This mismatch is contractually mitigated at closing via a Subscription mechanism, reimbursement options, and an arbitration fallback. Because TEPPCO retains both the operating processes and the existing workforce to run the system, there is no structural mismatch between operations and organization (gap_56).

grok.rationale: The slice documents that Enterprise 'finances and builds the new asset while the operating processes and personnel that run the system remain with Jonah/TEPPCO' (Exhibit 99.1 Sections 1(b), 2, 4), so the expansion capacity (T4) is placed into the co-ownership structure without the operating processes (T5) moving with it (gap_45=1). Operating processes and workforce are kept together under Jonah ordinary-course covenants to preserve officers, employees, and customer relationships (Section 4), yielding no T5-vs-T6 mismatch (gap_56=0). The LOI contractually bridges the mismatch via the Subscription, TEPPCO reimbursement option up to 100%, and arbitration fallback (Sections 1(b)-(e), 3).
